signals.title: Adversarial Social Epistemology for Assemblies of Humans and Large Language Models
signals.summary: We outline an adversarial social epistemology (ASE) for densely interactive communicative landscapes in which public assertions are scaffolded by chains of testimony, inference, institutional certification, and tacit trust. In such landscapes, agents have incentives and affordances to distort, color, omit, fabricate, or strategically under-specify information for private, reputational, rhetorical, or material gains.
signals.implication: Reassess role boundaries and human override for community deployments. Prioritize provenance checks and misinformation/abuse response protocols. Update constitutional clauses and compliance mappings for community operators. High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: This paper introduces an adversarial social epistemology (ASE) framework aimed at understanding communication dynamics involving both humans and large language models. It highlights the complexity of public assertions, which are built upon interconnected testimonial chains, inference, institutional validation, and implicit trust. The authors emphasize the potential for distortion, omission, or strategic manipulation of information, driven by the incentives individuals have to gain private, reputational, or material advantages. This perspective sheds light on the challenges that arise in environments where multiple agents interact, revealing vulnerabilities in how information can be misrepresented or misinterpreted. Understanding these dynamics is crucial for communities keeping up with AI as it underscores the need for robust information governance and ethical considerations in AI interactions.

signals.title: Structured Pruning of Large Language Models via Power Transformation and Sign-Preserving Score Aggregation with Adaptive Feature Retention
signals.summary: This paper proposes an improved structured pruning method for large language models (LLMs) that addresses key challenges in adapting Adaptive Feature Retention (AFR), an unstructured pruning technique, to structured pruning. When applying AFR to structured pruning, three major problems arise: distribution mismatch between heterogeneous pruning scores, loss of sign information indicating optimization direction consistency, and influence of outliers.
signals.implication: High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: This paper presents an enhanced structured pruning method for large language models (LLMs) that effectively tackles significant challenges in implementing Adaptive Feature Retention (AFR), originally an unstructured pruning approach, within structured pruning contexts. The authors identify three main issues during this adaptation: the distribution mismatch among different pruning scores, the loss of sign information that reflects direction consistency in optimization, and the impact of outliers on performance. By addressing these challenges, the proposed method aims to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of pruning in LLMs, which is crucial for optimizing model performance while reducing resource requirements. Understanding advancements like this is essential for the community as they highlight ongoing efforts to make powerful AI models more efficient and accessible.

signals.title: Overthinking: Amplifying Reasoning Weights to Extract Learned Secrets
signals.summary: Black box auditing of language models is an essential pre-deployment tool, but it may miss subtle forms of misalignment and hidden information. To better elicit hidden information during an auditing process, we introduce \emph{overthinking}: the process of using reasoning task vectors to amplify the propensity to think out loud of reasoning models.
signals.implication: Reassess role boundaries and human override for community deployments. Update constitutional clauses and compliance mappings for community operators. High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: The paper discusses a method called "overthinking," which aims to enhance the black box auditing of language models. Traditional auditing may overlook subtle misalignments and concealed information. The proposed overthinking technique utilizes reasoning task vectors to increase the likelihood that reasoning models will express their thought processes aloud, thereby aiding in revealing hidden information during audits. This research emphasizes the need for more effective auditing tools in the evaluation of language models, particularly in detecting nuanced issues that could lead to misalignment. Understanding such techniques is vital for communities engaged with AI, as it highlights the importance of ensuring the reliability and transparency of AI systems before they are deployed.

signals.title: Agentic AI and Retrieval-Augmented Models in Straight-Through Underwriting
signals.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to reshape actuarial practice, particularly in domains that require reasoning over unstructured documents, heterogeneous data sources, and regulated decision workflows. Actuaries now face a design space that ranges from traditional rule-based automation to large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and multi-agent ``agentic'' systems that plan, retrieve, call tools, and reflect.
signals.implication: Reassess role boundaries and human override for community deployments. Update constitutional clauses and compliance mappings for community operators. High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: Artificial intelligence is transforming actuarial practice by enabling improved decision-making in areas that involve reasoning with unstructured documents, various data sources, and regulated workflows. Actuaries are now exploring a range of technological options, from traditional rule-based automation to advanced approaches like large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and multi-agent "agentic" systems, which can plan, retrieve information, utilize tools, and reflect on processes. This evolution in technology highlights significant advancements that could streamline actuarial tasks and enhance efficiency in decision-making. Understanding these developments matters for our community as they signify a pivotal shift in how AI can be integrated into professional practices, emphasizing the importance of staying informed about AI's impact on traditional fields.

signals.title: Alignment Plausibility: A New Standard for Assuring AI in Healthcare
signals.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have become significant providers of mental health support, yet they remain products of an attention economy whose operational and commercial targets favour sustained engagement over the friction that effective psychological support often requires. Developers' safety responses have been largely reactive, addressing the most visible and acute harms while subtler, longer-term patterns of risk (e.g., dependency, boundary erosion, the amplification of distorted beliefs) receive less attention.
signals.implication: Update constitutional clauses and compliance mappings for community operators. High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly serve as providers of mental health support, but their design and operational goals often prioritize ongoing user engagement rather than the friction that effective psychological help necessitates. While developers have implemented safety measures, these responses mainly target immediate and obvious harms. As a result, more nuanced and long-term risks associated with LLM use, such as user dependency, erosion of boundaries, and the reinforcement of incorrect beliefs, are not adequately addressed. This highlights a critical gap in the safety and ethical governance of AI in healthcare, raising concerns about the potential for these technologies to inadvertently cause harm over time. Understanding these issues is crucial for the community to navigate the complexities of AI in mental health support and ensure responsible development practices.

signals.title: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
signals.summary: Nous Research , the open-source artificial intelligence startup backed by crypto venture firm Paradigm , released a new competitive programming model on Monday that it says matches or exceeds several larger proprietary systems — trained in just four days using 48 of Nvidia's latest B200 graphics processors . The model, called NousCoder-14B , is another entry in a crowded field of AI coding assistants, but arrives at a particularly charged moment: Claude Code , the agentic programming tool from rival Anthropic, has dominated social media discussion since New Year's Day, with developers posting breathless testimonials about its capabilities .

signals.long_summary: Nous Research has launched NousCoder-14B, a new open-source coding model that reportedly matches or exceeds the performance of several larger proprietary systems. signals.title: Salesforce rolls out new Slackbot AI agent as it battles Microsoft and Google in workplace AI
signals.summary: Salesforce on Tuesday launched an entirely rebuilt version of Slackbot , the company's workplace assistant, transforming it from a simple notification tool into what executives describe as a fully powered AI agent capable of searching enterprise data, drafting documents, and taking action on behalf of employees. The new Slackbot, now generally available to Business+ and Enterprise+ customers, is Salesforce's most aggressive move yet to position Slack at the center of the emerging "agentic AI" movement — where software agents work alongside humans to complete complex tasks.
